newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen sees 97 low close, other China stocks up.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen sees 97 low close, other China stocks up.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index posted its lowest close of 1997 on Wednesday, dragged down by a newly listed steel firm, but China's other share indices rose on a slight brightening in sentiment.
Shenzhen's Hong Kong dollar-denominated B share index was pulled down by the weighty Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd, which listed 400 million B shares on Tuesday.
The B index sagged 0.87 points or 0.71 percent to 120.44, after hitting a 1997 all-time low of 118.69 points. Turnover shrank to HK$94.0 million from HK$287.9 million on Tuesday.
Despite the fall on Wednesday, analysts said the B index was likely to hold steady in the near future.
"Bengang is the most heavily weighted stock in the B share market, and its poor performance today significantly dragged down the index," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
On Wednesday, Bengang plunged HK$0.15 or 6.38 percent to HK$2.20. Trading volume reached 23 million shares worth HK$50.8 million.
Shenzhen's domestic currency A shares gained on Wednesday on the back of market leader Shenzhen Development Bank, which rose 0.93 yuan or 2.8 percent to 34.0 yuan.
The A share index gained 5.17 points or 1.35 percent to 387.44. Turnover was 4.7 billion yuan against Tuesday's 5.3 billion.
Shanghai's foreign currency B shares surged 3.4 percent on Wednesday as investors went bargain hunting following a sharp 3.8 percent fall in the index the previous session.

Market sentiment received a shot in the arm on Wednesday after official newspapers carried comments from the State Planning Commission saying China's economic situation had been good throughout the first half of 1997.
The B index rose 2.422 points or 3.40 percent to 73.726 points on volume of 9.235 million shares worth $5.357 million.
Of 45 B shares, 41 traded with 29 up, six down and six flat.
"Market sentiment has improved somewhat," said a broker at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai.
"After panic selling over the past few days, some shares expected to post good results but at low price levels attracted buying, especially from domestic retail investors," she said.
Hua Xin Cement Co was the top B share gainer due to a technical rebound. It soared $0.016 or 10.13 percent to $0.174.
Shanghai's domestic currency A share index also rose on improved sentiment but brokers said investors remained cautious.
The A share index rose 10.957 points or 0.94 percent to 1,171.201 points on volume of 304.433 million shares worth 3.432 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index gained 40.311 points or 1.10 percent to 3,714.022 points.

Despite the rises in Shanghai on Wednesday, market sentiment remained fragile and uncertainty over upcoming interim results and possible government moves to keep the markets stable were likely to cap sharp gains, brokers said.
